what_its_for: Darolutamide is used to treat prostate cancer that has not yet spread to other parts of the body (called non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). It works by blocking the effects of male hormones (like testosterone) that help prostate cancer cells grow.
how_to_take: Take darolutamide by mouth WITH food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take your dose at the same times each day to help you remember. You will usually take this medicine along with another medicine called a GnRH analog (a hormone shot your doctor prescribes).
dosing: The usual dose is 2 tablets (600 mg total) taken TWICE a day — once in the morning with food and once in the evening with food. That means you take 4 tablets total each day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but ONLY if it is still the same day you missed it. If you did not take your dose that day, skip the missed dose completely and take your next regular dose the following day at the normal time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store darolutamide at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking darolutamide with certain other medications without your doctor's approval, as some drugs can make darolutamide work less well or increase side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take — especially rifampin, St. John's Wort, or certain seizure medications. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant must not handle crushed or broken tablets. Men taking darolutamide should use effective birth control with their partner during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: sudden severe headache, confusion, vision changes, or seizures; signs of a heart problem such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or swelling in your legs; severe tiredness or weakness that affects your daily life; falls or problems with balance; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Darolutamide starts working right away in your body, but you may not feel any different at first because it is fighting cancer at a cellular level. Your doctor will monitor how well the medicine is working through regular PSA blood tests and imaging scans. It is very important to keep taking your medicine every day even if you feel well.
special_populations: Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to lower your dose if you have moderate-to-severe kidney or liver problems. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions before starting this medicine. Older adults: Darolutamide has been safely used in older adults, but falls and fatigue may be more common, so use caution. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not approved for use in women, but women who are pregnant or breastfeeding must not handle crushed or broken tablets. Men with female partners who are pregnant or could become pregnant must use condoms during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
